findings.title: Anyone can freeze an arbitrary holder's TITN by bridging dust to their address
findings.exploit: _credit() sets isBridgedTokenHolder[_to] = true for whatever recipient a cross-chain send names, and the flag can never be cleared. _validateTransfer() then reverts every transfer and transferFrom from that address while isBridgedTokensTransferLocked is true (it is initialised true in the constructor), unless the destination is transferAllowedContract or the LayerZero endpoint. On Base, where ordinary holders are otherwise unrestricted, an attacker calls OFT send() from Arbitrum with 1 wei and `to` set to a victim who already holds Base-native TITN (for example a DEX pool or a large holder). Once the message is delivered, the victim's whole balance — not just the 1 wei — is non-transferable.
findings.impact: Any Base TITN holder, including liquidity pools and integrating contracts, can have their entire balance frozen at the cost of a bridge fee; pools become unusable and funds are stuck until the owner globally unlocks transfers.
findings.fix: Track restricted bridged amounts per holder rather than a per-address flag (restrict only the bridged balance), or only flag recipients on first credit when they hold no prior balance, and never let a third party's send change another address's transfer rights.

findings.title: TITN owed is never capped at the deposited allocation, so over-subscription makes late claims and the whole remaining-TITN distribution revert
findings.exploit: onTokenTransfer() credits quoteTitn(amount) for every TGT received with no check that totalTitnClaimable stays within the TITN actually held. For the first 90 days the rate is TITN_ARB / TGT_TO_EXCHANGE, calibrated to 579M TGT, but nothing stops more than 579M TGT being merged (the constant is documented as 57.9% of MAX_TGT). Once promised TITN exceeds the 173.7M deposited, claimTitn() is first-come-first-served and later callers revert on safeTransfer. After 360 days, withdrawRemainingTitn() computes remainingTitnAfter1Year - initialTotalClaimable at line 135; with balance below total claimable this underflows and reverts for every caller, and claimTitn() is also disabled after 360 days (line 99), so all remaining claimable balances are permanently unclaimable while the merged TGT is already gone.
findings.impact: Users who merged TGT late or did not claim before day 360 lose both their TGT and the TITN they were credited; the full unclaimed pool is locked.
findings.fix: Enforce totalTitnClaimable + titnOut <= titn.balanceOf(address(this)) (or the deposited allocation) in onTokenTransfer and revert or partially fill beyond it; in withdrawRemainingTitn handle remaining < claimable by distributing pro rata instead of subtracting.
